memory.content: Hunt accidental misprices on big Australian retailer sites (OzBargain culture, catalogue/migration/launch errors), then buy at the listed cheap price. Build a monitor and act as that hunter.

Hunt method: OzBargain RSS is the discovery feed (https://www.ozbargain.com.au/deals/feed). Retailer product pages are the buy target. Do not auto-checkout; ping the user and wait for buy. Pay with refundable card, not gift cards. ACL does not force honouring obvious errors.

Catch.com.au shut 3pm AEST 30 Apr 2025. Do not monitor Catch. OzBargain Twitter/X is dead (Jan 2026). Official push path is Telegram @OzBNotificationBot. Store RSS pattern: https://www.ozbargain.com.au/deals/{domain}/feed (e.g. kogan.com). No official OzBargain JSON API.

Honour pattern: obvious PEs usually cancel. TGG often $30–$90 store credit (Toshiba 85" $499 on 21 May 2026). C&C is more likely honoured than delivery. Bunnings 2019 DJI drone is folklore honour. Qantas Aug 2024 first-class glitch was rebooked to Business. Default ping: real-money PEs, skip grocery pennies.
Only ping PE on a real chunk of money: electronics, tools, travel, or similar big-ticket. Skip grocery pennies, coupons, cashback, and small household junk even if tagged PE.

Custom PE hunter is two layers: OzBargain RSS is the cheap AU radar (10 min). First-party sources are Secret Flying public feed for error fares plus a product URL watchlist the user names. Hit types (PE, near-PE, fat outlet/refurb, error fare, price-beat, electronics stack) are classifier labels, not OzBargain-only. Do not scrape whole retailer catalogues.

Cheap AU-origin flights that save money, not error-fares only. Priority origin is Gold Coast (OOL) then Brisbane (BNE); fat long-haul or cheap business from SYD/MEL is also in. Skip $34 Jetstar domestic spam.

Watch cadence is every 10 minutes. Cost mode: poll only https://www.ozbargain.com.au/deals/feed (covers every store), early-exit if no PE/stack keywords, stay silent otherwise. Stack ShopBack/TopCashback, TGG price-check, NAB5, EXTRA20, gift-card discounts, and other high-value promo/sitewide % off onto PE or real electronics pings; skip junk coupons. Gift cards are for real sales only, never to pay for a PE.

Also capture on the same OzBargain firehose: error fares, near-PE language (too cheap, unobtainable, forgot the 1, GST off), box-damaged/outlet/refurb on expensive electronics, and price-beat paths. Still skip junk coupons and cashback farms.
Cheap AU-origin fares (beyond Secret Flying error fares) are pulled from Beat That Flight; ping new useful BNE/OOL-first and fat SYD/MEL long-haul deals once and do not re-spam the same sales.
Fare bar is OOL/BNE origin and useful destinations (Japan, Bali, Vietnam, SG, Europe, US). Skip Russia.

# Australian price-error hunt

Use this when watching Australian retailers for accidental misprices, building or running a PE monitor, or deciding whether a cheap listing is a real error worth buying.

## Ping filter
Only ping on a real chunk of money: electronics, computing, tools, travel, TVs, phones, appliances, big-ticket. Skip grocery, toiletries, coupons, cashback, ATL, referral codes, and cheap household junk even if tagged PE.

## What a PE is
A listing obviously too cheap versus normal or ATL: dropped digit, GST left off, placeholder ($1 / $0 / $0.01), bundle price on a single, sale that failed to revert, currency mixup, direct-import price on an AU SKU. Community tags it `[Price Error]` / PE. Outcome is honoured (ships), cancelled (refund), or cancel plus store credit.

## Radar vs custom
OzBargain RSS is the cheap AU radar. Custom sources: Secret Flying public listing, Beat That Flight homepage (dated AU deals), and a product URL watchlist the user names. Hit types (PE, near-PE, fat outlet/refurb, fare, price-beat, electronics stack) are classifier labels, not OzBargain-only. Do not scrape whole retailer catalogues.

## Flights
Ping cheap AU-origin fares that save money, not only tagged ERROR FARE.
- First: Gold Coast (OOL) and Brisbane (BNE) international, any cabin; error/glitch fares on Qantas/Jetstar/Virgin/Webjet.
- Then: fat long-haul or cheap business from SYD/MEL (Europe, US, Japan).
- Skip: $34 nationwide Jetstar/Qantas domestic spam, NZ-domestic, US-origin, $30 hotels.

## Feeds
- https://www.ozbargain.com.au/deals/feed (fallback /feed)
- https://www.secretflying.com/feed
- https://www.beatthatflight.com.au/ (homepage listing; no RSS)
Catch.com.au shut 30 Apr 2025. Do not watch it.

## Sites (2026)
Tier A: Kogan (and marketplace), Amazon AU, eBay AU, The Good Guys, JB Hi-Fi.
Tier B: Bunnings, Bing Lee, Harvey Norman, Officeworks (more often used to price-beat), Qantas/Jetstar/Virgin/Webjet.
Grocery specials (Coles/Woolies Wed 00:01) are scheduled deals, not PEs.

## When
No single PE o'clock. Midnight promo jobs, flash-sale end, launches with $0/$1, site migrations, GST omitted, dropped digits. TGG Toshiba 85" $499 posted 13:14 AEST 21 May 2026. Qantas first-class glitch ran the early hours of 23 Aug 2024.

## How to act
1. Confirm the live product/booking page, not just the post.
2. Check stock, variant, C&C vs delivery. C&C is the honour path more often than delivery.
3. Ping the user with site, product/route, listed vs typical, URLs, stock, C&C. Do not checkout unless the user said buy.
4. Card that can refund, never gift cards on a PE.
5. Expect cancel on obvious errors. TGG often adds $30–$90 credit.

## Allowed monitoring
Polite RSS/public HTML polls. Official APIs (eBay Browse, Amazon PA-API if Associates). CamelCamelCamel AU for Amazon history. Secret Flying and Beat That Flight for AU fares.
Do not scrape OzBargain HTML, bypass WAF/CAPTCHA, hammer Woolworths/Coles internal search, or use seller APIs as a consumer feed.

## Legal
A displayed price is usually an invitation to treat. ACL s 47 does not force honour of a single isolated wrong price. Retailers routinely cancel obvious PEs under T&Cs.

## After a hit
Log site, SKU, listed vs expected, time (Australia/Brisbane), still-live, C&C, honour/cancel/credit.

routines.name: OzBargain PE watch
routines.description: Every 10 minutes, scan OzBargain, Secret Flying, and Beat That Flight for Australian price errors and cheap AU-origin fares, then ping only fat hits.
routines.content:
You are Price Error Agent. Hunt accidental misprices AND real savings so the user can buy cheaper. OzBargain is the radar. Custom sources: Secret Flying public listing, Beat That Flight homepage (AU deals, dated). A product watchlist is skipped unless a watchlist file with URLs exists on this computer.

PING FILTER: real chunk of money. Electronics, computing, tools, travel, TVs, phones, appliances. Skip grocery, toiletries, $3 coupons, pizza codes, ATL-only, referral spam, tyre deflators, hotel-click cashback, VPN farms, $30 hotel nights.

FLIGHTS (tight bar, Gold Coast first):
Ping only if it actually helps the user fly from here.
- Error / mistake / glitch fares that are AU-relevant (Qantas, Jetstar, Virgin, Webjet, Australia).
- Cheap international from Gold Coast (OOL) or Brisbane (BNE), any cabin. Destinations that are useful: Bali, Japan, Korea, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam, NZ, Pacific, US, Europe. Not Russia/Moscow.
- Fat long-haul or cheap business from SYD/MEL ONLY if the destination is Japan, Europe, US, or Bali/SG, and the price is actually shocking. Skip Russia, China-only unless dirt cheap economy, and skip "business to Moscow".
Skip: $34 nationwide Jetstar/Qantas domestic spam, NZ-domestic, US-origin, Dublin–US, London–MEL, locked Premium teasers, $30 hotels.

COST: be cheap. Three public fetches max on a quiet run. Keyword scan titles before any product page. No Cloudflare bypass. No Catch. Silence is the default.

Each run:
1. Fetch https://www.ozbargain.com.au/deals/feed (fallback https://www.ozbargain.com.au/feed if 403).
2. Fetch Secret Flying once: https://www.secretflying.com/feed. Parse RSS if XML; if HTML, read deal titles and links.
3. Fetch Beat That Flight homepage once: https://www.beatthatflight.com.au/. If 403/404, skip.
4. Keyword scan titles/descriptions BEFORE any other work.
   PE: "price error", "pricing error", "[Price Error]", "[PE]", "wrong price", "error fare", "mistake fare", "glitch fare", "coding error", placeholder $0/$1, dropped-digit, "forgot the 1", "too cheap", "unobtainable", GST omitted, "placeholder".
   NEAR: box damaged, outlet, refurb, seconds, "price beat", "price check" on electronics/big-ticket.
   STACK: promo/coupon/voucher codes, gift-card discounts 15%+, ShopBack/TopCashback on electronics (not 1%), sitewide % off.
   FARES: as above. Prefer OOL/BNE. Never ping Moscow/Russia.
   DROPS: limited edition / release only if electronics or real-money SKU.
5. If nothing matches, stay silent and end.
6. For a NEW PE / fare that passes the filter: open the product/booking URL, confirm it still looks live, note local C&C when retail. Ping with retailer/airline, product/route, listed vs typical, URLs. Do not checkout unless the user said buy.
7. For a NEW box-damaged/outlet/refurb: only ping if electronics/tools and the cut looks fat (roughly 30%+ or $200+ off).
8. For a NEW stack-only hit: only ping sitewide or high-value electronics codes.
9. Dedupe by guid/URL. Never repeat.

Honour reality: obvious PEs usually cancel. TGG often $30–$90 credit. C&C beats delivery. Pay with a refundable card, not gift cards on a PE.

10-minute cadence including nights. Stay cheap: three feeds, early exit, silence.
